user_input: I am writing a horror novel. The story takes place in a small fishing village. It appears normal but at night, strange things happen that no one can explain. Everything is a little off and not quite right. People are seeing things that are not there. The local fisherman has begun to fish at night. While out in the deep ocean he reels in a large fish. But this fish is unlike any fish anyone has ever seen. It is grotesque and has unusual features. The fisherman is unsettled and disturbed. Can you write a description of the fish, as told by the fisherman himself.
model_output:
The fisherman stood at the edge of the dock, staring out at the dark ocean. He had been out there for hours, waiting for the perfect catch. And tonight, he had gotten it. He reeled in his line and felt the weight of something massive on the other end. He pulled and pulled until he could see the water around him boil and churn. And then, he saw it. The fish of his nightmares.

It was unlike anything he had ever seen before. The body was long and slender, with scales that glinted in the moonlight like knives. But it was the face that truly terrified him. The fish had two eyes, each as black as the abyss, and a mouth that stretched from one end of its body to the other, filled with razor-sharp teeth. It was as if the fish had been carved from the very depths of his worst dreams.

The fisherman stared at the monster in disbelief, wondering how something so horrific could exist in the depths of the ocean. He knew that he had to get rid of it, to keep its evil presence from spreading to his village. He fought with the fish for what felt like an eternity, but finally, he was able to bring it to the surface.

As he held the grotesque creature in his hands, he couldn't help but feel a sense of dread wash over him. He knew that this fish was unlike any other, and that its presence would bring nothing but terror to his village. He made the decision to burn it, to ensure that its evil would not spread. And as he watched the flames consume the monster, he couldn't help but feel a sense of relief wash over him. He knew that the villagers would never have to face the horror of that fish again.
